Glossary Term Definition chlorofluorocarbon Chlorine-containing compound that is used as a refrigerant. (CFC) circuit A refrigerant loop consisting of a compressor, condenser, and metering device along with associated piping and valves that contain a refrigerant. Some equipment that is multistage has multiple circuits—each one is operated and maintained separately and therefore should be tracked independently even if it is in the same piece of equipment. form factor The physical design and layout of the refrigeration unit, including its size, shape, and how it's accessed. global warming Measure of warming impact of a compound relative to the same quantity potential (GWP) of carbon dioxide (CO ) over a certain number of years. A refrigerant 2 with a global warming potential of 1,000 will have 1,000 times the heat- trapping potential of CO . 2 hydrofluorocarbon Fluorinated-based compound that is an effective refrigerant because it has (HFC) properties that allow the phase change to occur at relatively low pressures and temperatures that are appropriate for heating, ventilating, and air- conditioning applications. monoblock system A self-contained refrigeration unit in which all major components are housed in a single, integrated piece of equipment. natural refrigerants A class of refrigerants that are non-synthetic, can exist naturally, and are not derived as a manufactured product. Examples include carbon dioxide, hydrocarbons, propane, and ammonia. ozone depletion Measure of ozone degradation of a compound compared to potential (ODP) trichlorofluoromethane (R-11), which has an ozone depletion potential of 1. refrigerant A two-phase working fluid that has thermodynamic properties that allow it to move heat from one location to another. refrigerant charge Amount of refrigerant in a refrigeration system. refrigeration Process that uses refrigerant to move heat from one space to another. split system A heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning system that has both an indoor and outdoor unit, requiring field-installed refrigerant piping connecting the indoor and outdoor units. working fluid A liquid or gas that transfers heat. 12 This report
